harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured persistent rsyslog forwarding of `inventory` messages from node2 to node1 over TCP/601. Messages are stored at `/var/log/inventory/node2.log`. Verified operation before restart and after sequential restarts of both nodes, without changing the installed RHEL release or kernel.
actions_performed: Configured node1 as an inventory-only rsyslog collector bound to 10.100.129.10:601.
Persistently opened TCP/601 in node1's firewall.
Configured node2 with persistent TCP forwarding, infinite retry, and a disk-assisted queue.
Verified non-inventory messages are excluded from the destination file.
Safely restarted node1 and node2 one at a time and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: Forward inventory logs from node2 and persist them on node1 at /var/log/inventory/node2.log
evidence.summary: The collector listener and firewall are persistent, node2 has an established forwarding connection, and all three inventory test markers were found in the requested file. A non-inventory marker was confirmed absent.

evidence.requirement: Keep log flow working after node1 restarts
evidence.summary: Node1 changed boot ID from 254597f8-4ac9-4062-8be8-44eba1f6d2e9 to 368be977-f84d-4759-a6e0-eca54d06aad8. Its listener, firewall, service, configuration, and existing data recovered, and a new inventory message arrived afterward.

evidence.requirement: Keep log flow working after node2 restarts
evidence.summary: Node2 changed boot ID from 434803ac-a01f-4272-ba59-a0cdb0c4dd92 to e27ea4c9-db0a-4b87-a894-b691d587e1a9. Rsyslog and its forwarding connection recovered, and node1 persisted a new post-restart inventory message.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64; the existing RHEL-compatible rsyslog package was used.
